mainTopic: The seven מצוות of בני נח: additions, their source in the פסוק to אדם, and whether דינין is included
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא in which several תנאים add מצוות for בני נח beyond the basic seven: blood from a living animal, castration, כישוף and some kinds of כלאים. The גמרא then asks where the Noahide מצוות come from. רבי יוחנן reads them, word by word, out of the פסוק in which ה׳ commanded אדם in גן עדן. רבי יצחק's version swaps two of the hints, and two אמוראים give different sources for linking 'ויצו' to עבודה זרה. That leads to a practical question: is a גוי liable just for making an idol? רבא challenges this, and רב פפא answers him. Next the גמרא asks how דינין can be a מצוה of בני נח if a ברייתא says it was added for ישראל at מרה. Three answers fail before רבא says that ברייתא follows תנא דבי מנשה, whose list has no דינין. The amud ends with a dispute about what אדם was commanded, and with the start of an explanation of where תנא דבי מנשה finds each of his seven מצוות.

steps.title: רבי חנניה בן גמלא adds blood from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניה בן גמלא says בני נח are also forbidden to consume blood taken from a living animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניה בן גמלא says: Non-Jews are also commanded not to eat blood taken from an animal that is still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of מצוות for בני נח, and רבי חנניה בן גמלא adds one more prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "also" tells us he accepts the basic list and adds to it. The basic list already forbids eating a limb from a living animal; he says blood taken from a living animal is forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Also concerning; adding an item to the list
Blood taken from a living animal
A תנא who adds this prohibition

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Gamla says:
Also concerning the blood from a living animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן גַּמְלָא אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל הַדָּם מִן הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא listing additional Noahide מצוות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני נח are forbidden to consume blood from a living animal.

steps.title: רבי חידקא adds castration
steps.stepSummary: רבי חידקא says בני נח are also forbidden to castrate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חידקא says: Non-Jews are also commanded not to castrate.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא adds another item to the list: בני נח may not castrate living creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the previous opinion, this is an extra prohibition on top of the basic seven. The list keeps growing, with each תנא adding one item.

keyTerms.meaning: Castration; making a living creature unable to reproduce
A תנא who adds castration to the list

phrases.english: Rabbi Chidka says:
Also concerning castration.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִידְקָא אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל הַסֵּירוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another addition to the list in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני נח are forbidden to castrate.

steps.title: רבי שמעון adds sorcery
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says בני נח are also forbidden to practice כישוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Non-Jews are also commanded not to practice sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds כישוף (sorcery) to the list of things forbidden to בני נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is one more addition. The next opinion, רבי יוסי, will widen this and give a source for it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Also concerning sorcery.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל הַכִּישּׁוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another addition to the list in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני נח are forbidden to practice כישוף.

steps.title: רבי יוסי includes every kind of sorcery
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that everything listed in the Torah's passage about כישוף is forbidden to בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Everything mentioned in the Torah's passage about sorcery is forbidden to a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי goes beyond רבי שמעון: not just plain sorcery, but every forbidden practice listed in the sorcery passage applies to בני נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון mentioned only כישוף. רבי יוסי includes the whole list in that passage of the Torah. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A descendant of Noah; any non-Jew

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Everything stated in the passage about sorcery,
a descendant of Noah is warned against it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָאָמוּר בְּפָרָשַׁת כִּישּׁוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רבי שמעון's addition of כישוף to the entire sorcery passage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All practices in the sorcery passage are forbidden to בני נח.

steps.title: The proof: the Canaanites were punished for these practices
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי quotes the פסוק listing sorcery practices and saying the nations were driven out because of them; since ה׳ punishes only after warning, these practices must have been forbidden to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says: "There shall not be found among you anyone who passes his son or daughter through fire, a diviner, a soothsayer, an enchanter, a sorcerer, a charmer, one who consults an אוב or ידעוני, or one who inquires of the dead... and because of these abominations ה׳ your God is driving them out before you." And ה׳ does not punish unless He first warned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי proves his rule: the Canaanite nations lost their land because of these practices, which means they were forbidden to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the nations were driven out because of these abominations. Punishment only makes sense if there was a prior warning. So every practice in this list must have been forbidden to the nations, meaning it is forbidden to all בני נח.

keyTerms.meaning: A diviner; one who predicts the future
A soothsayer and an enchanter (one who reads omens)
Types of necromancy; consulting spirits of the dead

keyTerms.term: לֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר
keyTerms.meaning: ה׳ does not punish unless He first warned

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "no punishment without a warning" is a tool for discovering prohibitions: if the Torah describes a punishment, there must have been a commandment behind it.

phrases.english: "There shall not be found among you
one who passes his son or his daughter through the fire,
a diviner, a soothsayer, an enchanter, or a sorcerer.
Or a charmer, or one who consults a necromancer or a wizard,
or one who inquires of the dead, etc.
And because of these abominations
the Lord your God is driving them out from before you."
phrases.notes: "Them" means the nations living in the land before the Jews came. They were not Jews, which is why this teaches about בני נח.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר.
phrases.english: And He does not punish unless He first warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עָנַשׁ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הִזְהִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and reasoning for רבי יוסי's rule
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's claim that all practices in the sorcery passage are forbidden to בני נח
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 18:10–12 combined with the principle that ה׳ punishes only after a warning

steps.title: רבי אלעזר adds mixed species, but only some kinds
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says בני נח are also commanded about כלאים, but only crossbreeding animals and grafting trees, not wearing mixed fabrics or sowing mixed seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Non-Jews are also commanded about mixed species. They may wear mixed fabrics and sow mixed seeds; they are forbidden only to crossbreed animals and to graft different trees together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds כלאים to the list, then immediately limits which kinds of כלאים apply to בני נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jews have several types of כלאים: clothing, seeds, animals and trees. רבי אלעזר says only two of them apply to non-Jews: breeding different animal species together and grafting different tree species. Wearing mixed fabric and sowing mixed seeds stay permitted for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Grafting one species of tree onto another

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אלעזר forbids all כלאים for non-Jews. He says "also כלאים" and then right away says wearing and sowing are permitted; only crossbreeding and grafting are forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Also concerning mixed species.
The descendants of Noah are permitted
to wear mixed fabrics and to sow mixed seeds,
and they are forbidden only
in crossbreeding animals and in grafting trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל הַכִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final addition to the list in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בני נח are forbidden to crossbreed animals and graft trees, but may wear mixed fabrics and sow mixed seeds.
steps.whatToRemember: Beyond the basic seven, different תנאים add: blood from a living animal (רבי חנניה בן גמלא), castration (רבי חידקא), sorcery (רבי שמעון, widened by רבי יוסי to the whole sorcery passage), and crossbreeding and grafting (רבי אלעזר).

steps.title: Where do the Noahide מצוות come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the מצוות of בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the Torah source of the Noahide מצוות. This sets up the next step, where רבי יוחנן answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we had only a list. Now the גמרא wants to know where in the תורה these commandments are found, since they were not given at סיני the way the Jews' מצוות were.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: "These matters" means the seven basic מצוות of בני נח listed earlier in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of additions to asking for the source of the basic מצוות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the מצוות of בני נח

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the command to אדם in גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the source is the פסוק where ה׳ commanded אדם in גן עדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because the verse says, "And the Lord God commanded the man, saying: Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins his answer by quoting the פסוק in which ה׳ gave אדם his first command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדם is the ancestor of all people, so commands given to him apply to all of humanity. In the lines that follow, the גמרא will show how individual words of this פסוק point to the different מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the famous derivation of all the Noahide מצוות from a single פסוק given to אדם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For the verse says,
"And the Lord God commanded the man, saying:
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:16

phrases.english: Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ה׳'s command to Adam in בראשית 2:16, which will be read word by word.

steps.title: 'And He commanded' points to the obligation to set up courts
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ויצו' hints at the מצוה of דינין (setting up courts). The proof is a פסוק about אברהם commanding his children to do justice.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And He commanded': this means the laws of justice. The Torah uses the word 'command' this way about אברהם: 'For I have known him, so that he will command his children,' to keep the way of ה׳ and to do justice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the פסוק about אדם word by word, as step 8 promised. The first word, 'ויצו', is matched to the מצוה of setting up courts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from where else the Torah uses the word 'command.' In the פסוק about אברהם, commanding his children leads to doing justice. So 'command' can point to justice, and here it hints at the מצוה of דינין.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of justice, meaning the duty to set up courts
And so it says. This brings another פסוק that uses the same word in the same sense.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first link in the chain that shows all seven מצוות of בני נח are hidden in one פסוק.

phrases.english: 'And He commanded': these are the laws of justice,
and so it says:
'For I have known him, so that
he will command his children, etc.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:19. The rest of the פסוק, hidden in 'etc.', talks about doing justice, and that's the link to courts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first part of רבי יוחנן's answer from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוה of דינין for בני נח
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 18:19, where 'command' is tied to doing justice

steps.title: 'ה׳', 'God' and 'the man' point to blasphemy, idol worship and murder
steps.stepSummary: 'ה׳' hints at ברכת השם, 'אלהים' hints at עבודה זרה, and 'על האדם' hints at שפיכות דמים. Each one is backed by a פסוק that uses the same word.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ה׳': this is cursing ה׳'s name, as it says, 'One who curses the name of ה׳ shall be put to death.' 'God': this is idol worship, as it says, 'You shall have no other gods.' 'The man': this is murder, as it says, 'One who sheds the blood of man,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with the next three words of the פסוק. Each word is matched to one more מצוה of בני נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method stays the same: find another פסוק where this word clearly shows up with that sin. ה׳'s name goes with the sin of cursing it. 'Gods' goes with idol worship. 'Man' goes with spilling a man's blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'blessing the Name.' It is a polite way of saying cursing ה׳.
One who curses or pronounces the Name to blaspheme

steps.confusionAlert: 'ברכת השם' does not mean blessing ה׳ in a good way. The גמרא is using a polite word for cursing ה׳, which is what the פסוק it quotes is about.

phrases.english: 'ה׳': this is 'blessing' the Name,
phrases.notes: The גמרא says 'blessing' to avoid saying 'cursing.' It really means cursing ה׳.

phrases.english: and so it says:
'And one who curses the name of ה׳ shall surely be put to death.'
'God': this is idol worship,
and so it says:
'You shall have no other gods.'
'Upon the man': this is murder,
and so it says:
'One who sheds the blood of man, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same word-by-word reading with the next three words.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוות of ברכת השם, עבודה זרה and שפיכות דמים for בני נח

steps.title: 'Saying', 'every tree' and 'you may eat' point to forbidden relations, stealing and a limb from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: 'לאמר' hints at גילוי עריות, proven from a פסוק in ירמיהו about a wife who leaves to another man. 'מכל עץ הגן' teaches no stealing, and 'אכל תאכל' teaches no אבר מן החי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Saying': this is forbidden relations, as it says, 'Saying: if a man sends away his wife, and she leaves him and becomes another man's.' 'From every tree of the garden': but not stolen things. 'You may surely eat': but not a limb from a living animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פסוק and finds the last three of the seven מצוות. That completes the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Saying' is tied to forbidden relations because the פסוק in ירמיהו opens with 'saying' and talks about a woman going to another man. The last two do not use an outside פסוק. The words themselves set a limit: eat from the garden's trees, which were given to you and not stolen, and eat in a permitted way, not a limb from a living animal.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb taken from a living animal

steps.whatToRemember: All seven מצוות of בני נח come from one פסוק to אדם: ויצו means courts, ה׳ means cursing ה׳‎, אלהים means idol worship, על האדם means murder, לאמר means forbidden relations, מכל עץ הגן means no stealing, and אכל תאכל means no limb from a living animal.

phrases.english: 'Saying': this is forbidden relations,
and so it says:
'Saying: if a man sends away his wife,
and she leaves him and becomes another man's.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:1

phrases.english: 'From every tree of the garden': but not stolen things.
'You may surely eat': but not a limb from a living animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the word-by-word reading and completes all seven מצוות.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוות of גילוי עריות, גזל and אבר מן החי for בני נח
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 3:1, plus the limiting words of the פסוק itself

steps.title: רבי יצחק's version swaps two of the hints
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יצחק arrived, he taught the reading with two hints reversed: 'ויצו' means עבודה זרה and 'אלהים' means דינין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יצחק came, he taught it the other way around: 'And He commanded' means idol worship, and 'God' means courts of justice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same reading. Only two words are switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of seven מצוות stays the same. What changes is which word hints at which מצוה: 'ויצו' now points to idol worship, and 'אלהים' points to courts. Everything else from steps 9-11 stays as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came. Usually this means arriving with a teaching from ארץ ישראל.
The reverse, the other way around

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יצחק does not argue about which seven מצוות בני נח have. He only switches which word of the פסוק teaches courts and which teaches idol worship.

phrases.english: When רבי יצחק came,
he taught it the reverse way:
phrases.notes: Only the first two hints get switched. The rest stays the same.

phrases.english: 'And He commanded': this is idol worship,
'God': this is courts of justice.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק תָּנֵי אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another version of steps 9-10 that switches two of the matches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יצחק's version, 'ויצו' teaches עבודה זרה and 'אלהים' teaches דינין.

steps.title: Where does 'ויצו' mean idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that 'אלהים' means דינין, but asks for the source that 'ויצו' means עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that 'אלהים' means courts, since the תורה calls judges 'האלהים'. But how do we know 'ויצו' means idol worship?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at רבי יצחק's reversed reading from step 12. It agrees with half of it and asks for a source for the other half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling judges 'אלהים' already has a clear פסוק behind it. But no פסוק has been shown yet that links the word 'ויצו' (commanding) to עבודה זרה. The גמרא wants that link.

phrases.english: Granted, "Elohim": this means courts of law,
as it is written: "And the master of the house shall come near to the judges."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:7. Here 'האלהים' clearly means the judges.

phrases.english: But "And He commanded": this means idol worship,
from where is that understood?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא ״אֱלֹהִים״ – זוֹ דִּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind part of רבי יצחק's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק linking the word 'ויצו' to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Two verses linking 'commanding' to idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב יצחק בר אבדימי each bring a different פסוק where a form of 'צו' appears together with idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: One brings the golden calf פסוק: 'They turned from the way I commanded them; they made themselves a calf.' The other brings: 'Ephraim is oppressed, because he willingly went after צו.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק puts 'צויתם' (I commanded them) right next to making the golden calf. The second uses the word 'צו' itself for the idol that Ephraim followed. Both tie the root 'צו' to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a word for something disgusting, meaning an idol

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi answer:
One said:
"They have turned aside quickly from the way
that I commanded them; they have made themselves, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:8, about the golden calf.

phrases.english: And the other said:
"Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment,
because he willingly went after filth (tzav)."
phrases.notes: הושע 5:11. 'צו' is the same root as 'ויצו', and here it means an idol.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי: חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the golden calf פסוק (שמות 32:8) or the Ephraim פסוק (הושע 5:11) links 'צו' to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What difference do the two verses make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether choosing one פסוק over the other changes anything in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking for a practical difference between the two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים prove the same basic point. So the גמרא wants to know if each one also leads to a different הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two answers in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the two sources lead to different rulings.

steps.title: Making an idol versus worshipping it
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a גוי who made an idol but did not bow to it. By the 'עשו' פסוק he is liable from the making; by the 'הלך' פסוק he is liable only once he worships it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is a גוי who made an idol but did not bow to it. The one who learns from 'they made' says he is liable as soon as he makes it. The one who learns from 'he went after' says he is not liable until he follows it and serves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each פסוק stresses a different act, so each one sets a different moment of liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The golden calf פסוק stresses 'עשו', making, so making alone is enough. The Ephraim פסוק stresses 'הלך אחרי', going after, so actual worship is needed.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
a gentile who made an idol
and did not bow to it.
According to the one who says "they have made",
he is liable from the moment of making it.
According to the one who says "because he willingly went",
he is not liable until he goes after it and worships it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גוי who made an idol but did not bow to it: liable according to 'עשו', not liable according to 'הלך'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step against the view that making alone makes a גוי liable.

steps.title: רבא challenges liability for just making an idol
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how anyone could hold a גוי liable for only making an idol. A ברייתא says a בן נח is warned only about those forms of עבודה זרה for which a Jewish court gives the death penalty, and that rule seems to leave out just making one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Does anyone really say a גוי who made an idol but did not bow to it is liable? A ברייתא teaches: With idol worship, whatever a Jewish court kills for, a בן נח is warned about. Whatever a Jewish court does not kill for, a בן נח is not warned about. What does that leave out? Isn't it a גוי who made an idol but did not bow to it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the first view from step 16 using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a בן נח's prohibitions in עבודה זרה only reach acts that would bring the death penalty for a Jew. רבא understands that this rule is meant to leave out simply making an idol. If so, the view that a גוי is liable from the moment of making seems to go against the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
A non-Jew, a descendant of Noach

phrases.english: Rava said:
And is there anyone who says

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁעָשָׂה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְלֹא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לָהּ – חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: that a gentile who made an idol and did not bow to it is liable?
But it was taught in a baraita: Regarding idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְמִיתִין עֲלֵיהֶן –
phrases.english: acts for which a Jewish court puts a person to death,
a descendant of Noach is warned about them;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְמִיתִין עֲלֵיהֶן –
phrases.english: acts for which a Jewish court does not put a person to death,
a descendant of Noach is not warned about them.
What is this meant to leave out?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו לְמַעוֹטֵי גּוֹי שֶׁעָשָׂה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְלֹא הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה לָהּ?
phrases.english: Isn't it meant to leave out a gentile who made an idol but did not bow to it?
phrases.notes: A Jew who only makes an idol does not get the death penalty, so רבא reads the rule as leaving this case out for a גוי too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first view in step 16, that a גוי is liable from the moment he makes an idol.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that learns from 'עשו', that a גוי is liable just for making an idol.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits a בן נח's עבודה זרה prohibitions to acts that bring the death penalty for a Jew. Making an idol without bowing does not, so a גוי should not be liable for it.

steps.title: רב פפא says the limit excludes hugging and kissing an idol
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers רבא. The ברייתא's limit to forms that carry the death penalty does not exclude making an idol. It excludes גיפוף ונישוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: No, that limit comes to exclude hugging and kissing an idol.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on רבא's question. He says the ברייתא's limit was never meant to exclude making an idol. It was meant to exclude hugging and kissing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a בן נח is not warned about anything a Jewish court does not punish with death, and רבא assumed that this rule is meant to leave out making an idol. רב פפא answers that the limit only removes hugging and kissing. So the opinion that a גוי is liable just for making an idol can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to leave out of the rule

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: No,
it comes to exclude hugging and kissing.
phrases.notes: He means that the ברייתא's limit to death-penalty cases is there to leave out hugging and kissing an idol, not making one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא, לְמַעוֹטֵי גִּיפּוּף וְנִישּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the ברייתא's limiting phrase excludes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limit to death-penalty forms excludes making an idol, so a גוי cannot be liable for just making one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit only excludes hugging and kissing, so liability for making an idol is still possible.

steps.title: What kind of hugging and kissing is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which hugging and kissing רב פפא means. If it is the idol's normal way of worship, that already carries the death penalty, so it could not be what is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hugging and kissing of what kind? If you say it is done in the idol's normal way of worship, then he deserves death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב פפא's answer by asking what kind of hugging and kissing he means. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any act done in an idol's normal way of worship carries the death penalty. So if this idol is normally worshipped by hugging and kissing, those acts cannot be the thing that is excluded. רב פפא must mean some other kind of hugging and kissing.

keyTerms.meaning: In its normal way, the usual way this idol is worshipped
If you say (the גמרא tries out one possibility)

phrases.english: Hugging and kissing of what kind?
If you say it is done in its normal way of worship,
then he deserves death!

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּיפּוּף וְנִישּׁוּק דְּמַאי? אִילֵּימָא כְּדַרְכָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind רב פפא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of hugging and kissing is excluded by the ברייתא.

steps.title: The exclusion is hugging and kissing that is not the idol's normal worship
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the exclusion covers hugging and kissing an idol that is not normally worshipped that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to exclude hugging and kissing that is not the idol's normal way of worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The excluded case is hugging and kissing an idol whose normal worship is something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hugging and kissing that is not the idol's normal worship does not carry the death penalty. So the ברייתא's limit leaves it out, and רב פפא's answer still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in its normal way of worship

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the ברייתא's limit to death-penalty forms only excludes hugging and kissing done in a way that is not the idol's normal worship. It does not rule out liability for making an idol.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to exclude when it is not done in its normal way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְמַעוֹטֵי שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The excluded case is hugging and kissing that is not the idol's normal way of worship.

steps.title: Were בני נח really commanded about courts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges listing דינין among the מצוות of בני נח. A ברייתא says ישראל received ten מצוות at מרה: the seven of בני נח, plus דינין, שבת and כיבוד אב ואם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Were בני נח commanded about courts? But a ברייתא teaches that ישראל were commanded ten מצוות at מרה: the seven that בני נח accepted, and on top of those, courts, שבת and honoring father and mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge. It asks how דינין can be one of the מצוות of בני נח when a ברייתא lists it as a מצוה added for ישראל at מרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counts the seven מצוות of בני נח and then names three more that were added. Since דינין is one of the three added ones, it seems it was not part of the seven. That clashes with the list that includes דינין as a מצוה of בני נח.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of justice; the מצוה to set up courts
The place where ישראל camped after the sea, before מתן תורה

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether ישראל must have courts. The question is whether דינין is one of the seven מצוות of בני נח.

phrases.english: Were the descendants of Noach commanded about courts?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Israel were commanded ten mitzvos at מרה:
the seven that the descendants of Noach accepted upon themselves,
and they added to them
courts, Shabbos, and honoring father and mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינִין בְּנֵי נֹחַ אִיפְּקוּד? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of making an idol and opens a new challenge about the list of מצוות of בני נח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inclusion of דינין in the seven מצוות of בני נח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא counts דינין among the מצוות added at מרה beyond the seven of בני נח, so it seems it was not one of the seven.

steps.title: The ברייתא's sources that these מצוות were given at מרה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows from פסוקים that דינין, שבת and כיבוד אב ואם were given at מרה. רב יהודה explains that 'כאשר צוך' means 'as you were commanded at מרה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Courts, as it is written: 'There He made for them a statute and a judgment.' שבת and honoring father and mother, as it is written: 'As ה׳ your God commanded you.' And רב יהודה said: 'As He commanded you' means at מרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives a source for each added מצוה, proving it was given at מרה. This strengthens the challenge against counting דינין as a מצוה of בני נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'משפט' in the פסוק about מרה is the source for דינין. In the עשרת הדברות, the words 'כאשר צוך' by שבת and כיבוד אב ואם show they had already been commanded earlier, and רב יהודה says that was at מרה. So דינין appears as something new for ישראל, not something בני נח already had.

keyTerms.meaning: As He commanded you, meaning an earlier command

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next move. It must explain how דינין can be one of the מצוות of בני נח if it was given at מרה.

phrases.english: Courts, as it is written:
"There He made for them a statute and a judgment."
phrases.notes: שמות 15:25. This פסוק is about מרה.

phrases.english: Shabbos and honoring father and mother, as it is written:
"As ה׳ your God commanded you."
phrases.notes: דברים 5:12 and 5:16. These words appear by both שבת and honoring parents in the עשרת הדברות.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
"As He commanded you" means at מרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינִין, דִּכְתִיב: שָׁם שָׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 21 by giving the פסוקים behind it.
steps.raayaObject: That דינין, שבת and כיבוד אב ואם were given to ישראל at מרה as additions beyond the seven מצוות of בני נח
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 15:25, 'שם שם לו חק ומשפט', and 'כאשר צוך' in דברים 5, as explained by רב יהודה

steps.title: First answer: מרה added the detailed rules of court procedure
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה answers the question from step 21. בני נח already had the basic מצוה of דינין. What was new at מרה was the detailed court rules: a full panel, witnesses and a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the new מצוה at מרה was only needed for the rules of a full court panel, witnesses, and a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question of how דינין can be both a מצוה of בני נח and something new at מרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic duty to have justice was already given to בני נח. At מרה, ישראל got extra procedures. A death case needs a full panel of judges, two witnesses, and a warning before the sin. So 'added at מרה' means added details, not a brand-new מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for. This is a phrase used to narrow what a source is really adding.
A full court panel (a סנהדרין of 23 judges for death cases)
A warning given to the sinner before he sins

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says that Rabba bar Avuh says:
It was necessary only
for a court panel, and witnesses, and forewarning.
phrases.notes: He means the מצוה given at מרה was only these extra court rules.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לָעֵדָה, וְעֵדִים, וְהַתְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 21 and supported in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope: the מצוה given at מרה was only extra procedural details
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that ישראל first received the whole מצוה of דינין at מרה
steps.terutzMaskana: בני נח had basic justice. מרה added the full panel, witnesses and warning.

steps.title: Details are not an added מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer. If מרה only added details, why does the ברייתא say 'they added דינין to them,' as if it were a new מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'and they added דינין to them' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר אבוה's answer using the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counts דינין as one of three extra מצוות beyond the seven. Details of a מצוה that already exists would not be listed as a separate added מצוה. So the wording does not fit this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your answer is right)
And they added to them (to the seven מצוות)

phrases.english: If so,
what is the meaning of "and they added to them: judgment"?
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from step 21, which lists דינין as a new מצוה on top of the seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי וְהוֹסִיפוּ עֲלֵיהֶן דִּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר אבוה's answer that מרה only added procedural details
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא presents דינין as a new מצוה added to the seven, not as details of an existing one

steps.title: Second answer: מרה added the laws of fines
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. What was new at מרה was the laws of fines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: it was only needed for the laws of fines.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer failed, רבא offers a new answer about what was added at מרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fines (קנסות) are not part of basic justice. They are an extra payment placed on the guilty person. רבא says these were given only to ישראל at מרה, while בני נח had only basic justice.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of fines: set penalties that go beyond paying for actual damage
Rather. It drops the earlier answer and brings a new one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava says:
It was necessary only for the laws of fines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְדִינֵי קְנָסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new limit on what מרה added: a separate area of law (fines)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Procedural details might explain the addition, but they are not a new מצוה
steps.terutzMaskana: מרה added the laws of fines, which בני נח never had

steps.title: The wording still does not fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבא too. If fines were added, the ברייתא should have said 'they added in דינין,' meaning more laws within the area of judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, it should have said 'and they added in דינין'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's answer also does not match the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fines are a new set of laws inside the area of judgment, not a new מצוה. So the wording should be 'added in דינין' (more court laws). It should not be 'added דינין' (the מצוה itself). The one-letter difference shows this answer is still too small.

keyTerms.meaning: And they added within דינין (more laws inside judgment)

phrases.english: Still,
it should have said: "and they added in judgment"!
phrases.notes: Look at the extra letter ב: 'in דינין' would mean more rules inside an existing מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכַּתִּי, וְהוֹסִיפוּ בְּדִינִין מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that מרה added the laws of fines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fines are more rules within judgment, so the ברייתא would have said 'added in דינין,' not 'added דינין'

steps.title: Third answer: courts in every province and city
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says what was new at מרה was the duty to set up a court in every province and every city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said: it was only needed to set up a court in every province and every city.
steps.whatsHappening: After two answers failed, רב אחא בר יעקב offers a third answer about what was added at מרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the addition is not details of how to judge. It is a new duty to set up courts all over the land. That can more easily be called an 'added' מצוה of דינין.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְהוֹשִׁיב בֵּית דִּין
phrases.english: It was necessary only to establish a court
in each and every province,
and in each and every city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְהוֹשִׁיב בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's answer, which was rejected in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new limit on what מרה added: a duty to set up courts everywhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fines might explain the addition, but they do not match the wording
steps.terutzMaskana: מרה added the duty to set up courts in every province and city

steps.title: But בני נח also had to set up courts everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב with a ברייתא. Just like ישראל, בני נח were also commanded to set up courts in every province and city. So this cannot be what was new at מרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But were בני נח not commanded about this? A ברייתא teaches: just as ישראל was commanded to set up courts in every province and every city, so too בני נח were commanded to set up courts in every province and every city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack the third answer. The next step shows how the גמרא gets out of this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב said courts everywhere was something only ישראל got at מרה. The ברייתא says בני נח had the very same duty, in the very same words. If so, this cannot be the addition at מרה.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely. It opens a challenge.
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: This step is still a challenge, not the conclusion. The ברייתא is brought to attack רב אחא בר יעקב's answer, and the גמרא's reply comes next.

phrases.english: And were the descendants of Noah not commanded about this?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
Just as the Jewish people were commanded
to establish courts

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל פֶּלֶךְ וָפֶלֶךְ וּבְכׇל עִיר וָעִיר,
phrases.english: in each and every province and in each and every city,
so too, the descendants of Noah were commanded
to establish courts

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל פֶּלֶךְ וָפֶלֶךְ וּבְכׇל עִיר וָעִיר.
phrases.english: in each and every province and in each and every city.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בְּנֵי נֹחַ לָא אִיפְּקוּד? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's answer from step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's claim that only ישראל was commanded to set up courts everywhere
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says בני נח had the exact same duty to set up courts in every province and city, so it cannot be what was new at מרה

steps.title: רבא: The מרה ברייתא follows תנא דבי מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the challenge from step 28. The ברייתא that says דינים were new at מרה follows תנא דבי מנשה, who does not count דינים among the מצוות of בני נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This תנא is the תנא of the school of מנשה, who takes out ד״ך (דינים and ברכת השם) and puts in ס״ך (סירוס and כלאים).
steps.whatsHappening: Since all three attempts to explain what was 'added' at מרה have failed, רבא takes a new approach to the original question from step 21. He says the ברייתא about מרה follows a תנא who holds that בני נח were never commanded about דינים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each attempt to explain the word 'added' kept assuming that בני נח had דינין. רבא says not every תנא agrees. תנא דבי מנשה leaves דינים off the list completely, so for him the whole מצוה of courts really was new at מרה, and the ברייתא's wording fits exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the school of מנשה, a source of ברייתות
Memory aid: ד for דִּינִים, ך for בִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם
Memory aid: ס for סֵירוּס, ך for כִּלְאַיִם

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that בני נח never have courts according to everyone. He is only saying which תנא the מרה ברייתא follows.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא תַּנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה הוּא,
phrases.english: This tanna is the tanna of the school of Menashe,
phrases.notes: "This תנא" means the one who taught that דינים were added at מרה.

phrases.english: who takes out dalet-kaf and puts in samekh-kaf.
phrases.notes: These are memory letters. ד״ך stands for דינים and ברכת השם, and ס״ך stands for סירוס and כלאים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי תַּנָּא תַּנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 28 knocks down רב אחא בר יעקב's answer, רבא drops all three attempts and answers the original challenge of step 21 a new way: the מרה ברייתא follows תנא דבי מנשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא with a different view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds that בני נח were commanded about דינים, so courts could not have been new at מרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מרה ברייתא follows תנא דבי מנשה, who leaves דינים out of the seven מצוות of בני נח.

steps.title: The School of Menashe's List of Seven מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the list from תנא דבי מנשה: עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, גזל, אבר מן החי, סירוס and כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of מנשה taught: בני נח were commanded seven מצוות: עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, שפיכות דמים, גזל, אבר מן החי, סירוס and כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual ברייתא of the school of מנשה to show the list רבא described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list still has seven items, but דינים and ברכת השם are missing and סירוס and כלאים take their place. That confirms that for this תנא, courts were not one of the מצוות of בני נח.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of Noach, meaning all of mankind
Mixing species (crossbreeding animals or grafting trees)
A limb taken from a living animal

phrases.english: As the school of Menashe taught:
The descendants of Noah were commanded seven מצוות:
idol worship, and forbidden relations,
and bloodshed, robbery,
and a limb from a living animal,
castration, and mixing species.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבא's claim in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That תנא דבי מנשה does not count דינים among the מצוות of בני נח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of מנשה listing seven מצוות without דינים and ברכת השם.

steps.title: What Was אדם Commanded?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says אדם הראשון was commanded only about עבודה זרה. רבי יהודה בן בתירה adds ברכת השם. The יש אומרים add דינים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: אדם הראשון was commanded only about עבודה זרה, as it says, "And ה׳ אלהים commanded the man." רבי יהודה בן בתירה says: also about ברכת השם. Some say: also about דינים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a three-way dispute about which מצוות אדם הראשון was given, all learned from the same פסוק. It also sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion reads more into the פסוק "ויצו ה׳ אלהים על האדם." רבי יהודה sees only עבודה זרה. רבי יהודה בן בתירה adds ברכת השם, and the יש אומרים add דינים as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'blessing the Name', a polite way of saying cursing ה׳

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Adam, the first man, was not commanded
except about idol worship alone,
as it says: "And the Lord God commanded the man."
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:16

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beseira says:
Also about blessing the Name.
phrases.notes: "Blessing" here is a polite way of saying cursing ה׳. The prohibition is against cursing Him.

phrases.english: And some say: also about laws of justice.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לֹא נִצְטַוָּוה אֶלָּא עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of בני נח מצוות to a dispute about what אדם הראשון was commanded from the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three views: only עבודה זרה; also ברכת השם; also דינים.

steps.title: Whose View Matches רב's Teaching on 'אלהים'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which view in the dispute fits רב's teaching that the word אלהים teaches three things: do not curse Me, do not exchange Me, and let My fear be upon you.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רב יהודה said in the name of רב: "I am אלהים": do not curse Me. "I am אלהים": do not exchange Me. "I am אלהים": let My fear be upon you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's דרשה on the word אלהים in the פסוק and asks which opinion from step 31 it matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads three lessons into one word. Not cursing matches ברכת השם, not exchanging matches עבודה זרה, and fear of ה׳ matches דינים. The question is which view includes all three.

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow,
that Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
"I am God": do not curse Me,
"I am God": do not exchange Me,
"I am God": let fear of Me be upon you?
phrases.notes: This is the part that matches דינים, since courts keep people in fear of ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion from step 31 fits רב's דרשה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא from the dispute about אדם הראשון agrees with רב's threefold reading of אלהים.

steps.title: It Follows the 'Some Say' Opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's teaching follows the יש אומרים, who include ברכת השם, עבודה זרה and דינים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? It follows the יש אומרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב follows the יש אומרים, the only view that includes all three lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה has only עבודה זרה, and רבי יהודה בן בתירה adds only ברכת השם. Only the יש אומרים also include דינים, which matches "let My fear be upon you."

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the opinion of 'some say'

steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק, "ויצו ה׳ אלהים על האדם," is the source for the מצוות given to אדם. רב's threefold דרשה on אלהים follows the יש אומרים, who include דינים.

phrases.english: Whose view? Like the "some say."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? כְּיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's דרשה follows the יש אומרים, who include ברכת השם, עבודה זרה and דינים.

steps.title: Where does the תנא דבי מנשה get his list from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא דבי מנשה with a two-sided question. If he expounds ויצו, he should also include ברכת השם and דינים. If he does not expound ויצו, he has no source for his seven מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about the תנא דבי מנשה: if he learns from the word "ויצו" (and He commanded), then he should count those two (ברכת השם and דינים) too. If he does not learn from "ויצו", where does he get these seven from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the list of the תנא דבי מנשה from step 30. It sets up a trap with two sides, and both sides seem to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main source for the מצוות of בני נח is the פסוק ויצו ה' אלהים על האדם, and that פסוק includes ברכת השם and דינים. So if the תנא דבי מנשה uses this פסוק, he should not leave those two out. But if he does not use it, his whole list seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the study house of מנשה, whose list of seven מצוות leaves out ברכת השם and דינים
He expounds, meaning he learns a law from the words of a פסוק
"And He commanded". This is the opening word of the פסוק that is the source for the מצוות of בני נח
From where does he know it? This asks for a source

steps.confusionAlert: "הנך" (those) and "הני" (these) mean different things here. "Those" are ברכת השם and דינים, which he left out. "These" are the seven מצוות on his own list.

phrases.english: And the תנא of the school of מנשה:
if he expounds "and He commanded"
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:16

phrases.english: then even those too should be included
phrases.notes: "Those" are ברכת השם and דינים, the two he left off his list.

phrases.english: and if he does not expound "and He commanded"
these, from where does he derive them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דָּרֵישׁ ״וַיְצַו״ – אֲפִילּוּ הָנָךְ נָמֵי, אִי לָא דָּרֵישׁ ״וַיְצַו״ – הָנֵי מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list of the תנא דבי מנשה from steps 29-30 and questions its source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of seven מצוות given by the תנא דבי מנשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided question. Using ויצו would force him to include ברכת השם and דינים. Not using ויצו leaves his list without any source.

steps.title: Each of his מצוות is written on its own
steps.stepSummary: The תנא דבי מנשה does not expound ויצו. Each of his seven מצוות has its own separate פסוק in the תורה. The גמרא begins listing them with עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does not learn from "ויצו". These seven, each one of them, are written separately: עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by picking the second side: he does not use ויצו. It then starts showing where each of his מצוות is written, starting with עבודה זרה and גילוי עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he never uses ויצו, he is not forced to include ברכת השם and דינים. He still has a source for his seven, because each one has its own separate פסוק. The sentence is cut off here, and the גמרא will now show those פסוקים one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. The גמרא uses this word to choose one side of the question
It is written in the תורה

phrases.english: Actually, he does not expound "and He commanded".
As for these, each and every one
is written on its own:
idol worship and forbidden relationships -

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לָא דָּרֵישׁ ״וַיְצַו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of step 34 by picking the side where he does not expound ויצו.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the question and gives a different source for his list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ויצו, the תנא דבי מנשה would have no source for his seven מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each of his seven מצוות has its own separate פסוק, so he does not need ויצו. That is also why he does not include ברכת השם and דינים.
